principles.statement: For penalty-aware TSP with carrot constraint, grid-guided 2-opt with penalty-aware fast delta + Or-opt + position tracking outperforms random swap + approximate boundary-only 2-opt by ~9 points (78.8 vs 69.5), because spatially-guided moves are more productive and exact penalty delta avoids accepting bad moves.
principles.regime: TSP with N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, penalty structure at every 10th position
principles.mechanism: Three synergistic improvements: (1) Grid-guided neighbor selection finds spatially close cities for 2-opt, so more moves are productive. (2) Penalty-aware fast delta computes exact cost change including penalty positions in O(1 + segment/10), avoiding the error accumulation of boundary-only delta. (3) pos[] array enables O(1) position lookup for NN-guided move selection. (4) Or-opt (single city relocate) handles improvements that 2-opt reversal cannot.
principles.applicability_bounds: Requires grid data structure and pos[] array maintenance. The improvement magnitude depends on time budget relative to N.

principles.statement: The penalty structure (10% surcharge on every 10th step when source is non-prime) contributes at most ~1% to total tour cost. Prime scheduling post-pass captures most available savings but adds <1 point to score.
principles.regime: N up to 200K with ~18K primes and ~N/10 penalty positions
principles.mechanism: With N/10 penalty positions and 10% surcharge per position, max penalty contribution is 10% * 10% = 1% of tour cost. Primes cover ~90% of penalty positions at max N, leaving limited room for optimization.
principles.applicability_bounds: Specific to this problem's penalty structure. Different penalty rates or prime densities would change the calculus.

principles.statement: For penalty-aware TSP under tight time limits (2s, N=200K), grid-guided spatial neighbor selection for 2-opt (using the same grid as NN construction, O(1) per lookup) outperforms both precomputed KNN lists (O(N*K) build overhead) and random selection, because it provides spatial guidance without startup cost.
principles.regime: TSP with N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, penalty structure at every 10th position
principles.mechanism: Grid-based neighbor lookup reuses the spatial grid built for NN construction. For each SA move, it picks a random city in the same or adjacent grid cell as the selected city, achieving spatial proximity (cities in same cell are geometrically close) without the O(N*K) cost of precomputing a KNN list for every city. For N=200K with K=12, KNN building takes 0.3-0.5s, which is 15-25% of the 2s budget. Grid lookup is O(1) amortized.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies when time budget is tight relative to N. For longer time limits or smaller N, precomputed KNN may be better because it provides exactly the K closest neighbors rather than random samples from nearby cells.

principles.statement: Double-bridge perturbation (non-sequential 4-opt) does NOT improve TSP score within a 2-second time limit for N=200K, because the overhead of O(N) tour recomputation after each perturbation plus shorter SA phases with cold restarts outweighs the benefit of escaping local optima.
principles.regime: TSP with N up to 200K, 2-second time limit, SA-based optimization
principles.mechanism: After double-bridge, totalCost() requires O(N) recomputation. For N=200K this costs ~5ms per perturbation. The SA phase after perturbation starts with a degraded tour that needs significant iterations to recover. Splitting the 1.75s SA budget into 0.4s phases means each phase barely converges before the next perturbation. The net effect is fewer total productive SA iterations compared to continuous SA.
principles.applicability_bounds: This refutation applies specifically to N=200K with 2s total time. For smaller N (where totalCost() is cheap) or longer time limits (where each SA phase can fully converge), double-bridge ILS may still be beneficial as in classical TSP literature.

principles.statement: Multi-city Or-opt (segments 1-3) with grid-guided insertion does not measurably improve score beyond single-city Or-opt for penalty-aware TSP at N=200K within 2s. The effect, if present, is below 0.2 points (~0.25% of score).
principles.regime: penalty-aware TSP, N=200K, 2s time limit, grid-guided 2-opt + Or-opt SA baseline scoring ~78.8
principles.mechanism: At the tour quality level achieved by grid-guided 2-opt + single-city Or-opt (~78.8), compound relocations of 2-3 cities rarely find improvements that single-city relocations miss. Grid-guided insertion targeting does not consistently select better positions than random shift, possibly because spatially-nearby cities are already tour-adjacent in a well-optimized tour.
principles.applicability_bounds: Applies to the specific move mix (55/10/35), SA temp (curCost/N*3), and grid-guided insertion strategy tested. A different Or-opt targeting strategy (e.g., nearest-neighbor in tour order) or tighter segment size selection might yield different results.
